findings.issue_text: [BUG] The login form's backupCode value never reaches the next-auth authorize callback: this diff adds backupCode to LoginValues (line 44) and registers the input via BackupCode.tsx, but updates neither the zod formSchema behind zodResolver (line 67, unchanged: `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })`) nor the signIn("credentials") call region (untouched between hunks), so the resolver strips the undeclared key from the values passed to the submit handler and credentials.backupCode in next-auth-options.ts:131 is undefined. Every backup-code login attempt falls into the TOTP branch, which throws SecondFactorRequired — a user who lost their authenticator is trapped in an infinite 2FA prompt and can never log in, while the DisableTwoFactorModal path (no resolver, so full form values flow) works, masking the break during manual testing.

[BUG] onEnable() and resetState() are wired only to the backup-codes Close button and the step-gated cancel button; the Dialog's onOpenChange path (header X, ESC, overlay click) runs neither, so dismissing the modal after a successful enable skips the parent notification and the internal state reset. A user who closes the backup-codes screen via X/ESC leaves the settings switch showing 2FA disabled while the backend has it enabled, and reopening the modal jumps straight to the stale DisplayBackupCodes step (cancel button is hidden on that step) showing the previous session's codes with no password confirmation; pre-diff onEnable() always fired on enable success, so this desync is introduced by this diff.

[ADVISORY] The missing_backup_codes message instructs users to "generate them in your settings", but no settings flow exists to generate backup codes — they are only created during the 2FA setup call (setup.ts:60-64), and every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy has backupCodes null. The installed base of 2FA users who lose their authenticator click "Lost access", get an instruction they cannot follow (generating codes requires disabling 2FA, which requires the TOTP they lost), and end at a permanent lockout with a misleading error message pointing at a nonexistent feature.

[ADVISORY] Backup-code consumption in authorize is a non-transactional read-modify-write — indexOf over the decrypted array followed by a separate prisma.user.update — so two concurrent logins presenting the same code both match at index before either write lands. A single backup code authenticates two sessions when requests race (double-submit or replay), violating the "used exactly once" guarantee the UI states in backup_code_instructions while both sessions are granted.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises the new backup-code authentication behavior — logging in with a backup code, consuming a code, or disabling 2FA with a code — as the TODO at line 13 admits; the added e2e assertions only cover the download/copy/close UI chrome of the codes dialog. A regression in the normalization (replaceAll), matching (indexOf), or null-consumption logic added to next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts ships silently — even a total failure of backup-code login passes CI, since no test ever submits a backup code to the auth endpoints.

[ADVISORY] BackupCode.tsx declares `export default function TwoFactor({ center = true })`, duplicating the component name of apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx in a copy-paste. The next maintainer grepping for TwoFactor or reading React DevTools/stack traces sees two distinct auth components both named TwoFactor, and future 2FA edits or imports land in the wrong file.

[BUG] The diff registers backupCode on the login form but never adds backupCode to the zod formSchema that zodResolver uses at line 67 (no hunk in this diff touches any zod schema), so zod's default strip mode removes the unknown key from the parsed values react-hook-form passes to handleSignIn and signIn("credentials") submits without backupCode. A user who clicks "Lost access" and submits a valid backup code gets credentials.backupCode === undefined in authorize(), falls into the TOTP branch, and receives SecondFactorRequired — backup-code login, the feature's core flow, silently dead-ends on the login page, and the new IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes handlers in handleSignIn are unreachable; the diff's own TODO admits this path is untested.

[BUG] resetState() and onEnable() are invoked only from the Close button, so dismissing the dialog at the DisplayBackupCodes step via Esc, the Dialog's built-in close affordance, or onOpenChange skips both — step state remains DisplayBackupCodes and the parent is never told 2FA was enabled. The settings switch stays unchecked while the server has 2FA enabled; because component state persists while mounted, reopening the modal drops the user straight onto the stale backup-codes screen with no password confirmation, and after the user disables 2FA and reopens, Close calls onEnable() so the UI shows 2FA enabled with the old codes while the server has twoFactorEnabled=false and backupCodes=null.

[ADVISORY] The MissingBackupCodes error is reachable only by legacy 2FA users (backupCodes column is null until this feature's setup runs), yet the accompanying message added in common.json ("No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.") instructs an action that does not exist — the only writer of backupCodes is setup.ts, which is reachable solely through the enable flow, and no settings path regenerates codes while 2FA is enabled. Every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy is dead-ended: the recovery feature provides them nothing, the error tells them to do something impossible without fully disabling 2FA (which itself requires the TOTP they have lost), and there is no backup-code rotation path for anyone once 2FA is on.

[BUG] Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt the array, null the index, re-encrypt and overwrite), so two concurrent authorize() calls both read the same stored array and both pass the indexOf check. A double-submit or two devices using the same code concurrently both get sessions from one code, violating the "each backup code can be used exactly once" promise the new locale string makes; worse, two devices burning two different codes concurrently each write from the same snapshot, resurrecting the other device's already-used code for later reuse.

[ADVISORY] The only test coverage this diff adds is the enable-flow display of backup codes (download filename, copy toast, close); the two new security-critical server paths — single-use consumption in next-auth authorize() and the backup-code branch of the disable endpoint — are exercised by no test, as the diff's own TODO ("add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup") concedes. A regression in either path (e.g. the login form never transmitting backupCode, or a bad index burn corrupting the stored array) ships silently; the download-content and clipboard-content TODOs also leave the actual backup codes displayed to users unverified, so a formatting bug in formatBackupCode would pass the suite.

[BUG] The lost-access/backup-code affordance is added only to TwoFactorFooter; the sibling ExternalTotpFooter (rendered for external-auth 2FA users on the same login page) is left without any backup-code entry point. Any user presented with ExternalTotpFooter who has TOTP enabled with stored backup codes has no way to enter one when they lose their authenticator — the lost-access recovery requirement is silently scoped to CAL-credential logins only.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a FIXME documenting that `expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` is vacuous — isChecked() returns a Promise, which is always truthy — and leaves the assertion broken instead of fixing it. The suite's only assertion that 2FA actually turned on after enable can never fail, so switch-state regressions (exactly the desync class this feature risks, cf. the onEnable-only-from-Close-button path) pass CI green.

[BUG] Backup-code comparison is case-sensitive (`backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`) against lowercase hex codes, with no toLowerCase() normalization — while the BackupCode input's own placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX" models uppercase entry. A user who correctly recalls their code but types the hex letters in uppercase (as the placeholder suggests) is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode on login, and the identical comparison in disable.ts (~line 61) burns a disable attempt the same way.

[ADVISORY] The copy button calls navigator.clipboard.writeText with no fallback or guard, and the Clipboard API is undefined in non-secure contexts. On a self-hosted instance accessed over plain http from a non-localhost host, clicking Copy throws an unhandled TypeError — nothing is copied and no toast appears, so users believe their codes are saved when they are not (the one-time codes are then unrecoverable until 2FA is re-enabled).

[ADVISORY] The default export of BackupCode.tsx is declared as `function TwoFactor({ center = true })`, giving two distinct components named TwoFactor that DisableTwoFactorModal and login.tsx import together and switch between. React DevTools, stack traces, and grep for "TwoFactor" show the TOTP component when a developer is debugging the backup-code path on this security-critical screen, raising the risk of editing or instrumenting the wrong component during the next change.

[BUG] The diff adds backupCode to LoginValues and registers the field in the form, but never adds backupCode to the zod formSchema that zodResolver (unchanged context at login.tsx:67) applies to every submission, so the parsed values handed to signIn("credentials") omit the key. authorize() never sees credentials.backupCode, always takes the TOTP branch, and returns SecondFactorRequired on every lost-access attempt — the backup-code login flow this PR builds can never authenticate, and the UI shows no error because SecondFactorRequired merely re-sets the already-true twoFactorRequired flag.

[BUG] The MissingBackupCodes error copy instructs users to "generate them in your settings", but this diff ships no settings UI or API that generates or regenerates backup codes — the only generator is the setup endpoint, which runs exclusively when starting a fresh 2FA enable. Users who hit this error (anyone who exhausted, lost, or was never given their codes) follow the instruction, find no such control anywhere in settings, and dead-end in the recovery flow this PR advertises; support intervention becomes the only exit.

[BUG] The single-use invariant this PR itself states in its shipped copy ("Each backup code can be used exactly once") is enforced as a non-atomic check-then-write: indexOf runs against the decrypted array and the nulled array is persisted in a separate unconditional prisma.user.update with no condition on the code. Two concurrent sign-ins submitting the same code both pass the indexOf check before either write lands, so the code authenticates twice (or N times in a burst) while the updates clobber each other — a replayed/phished code keeps working in the race window regardless of the victim consuming it.

[ADVISORY] The migration adds backupCodes as a nullable column with no backfill, so every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy keeps backupCodes null and has no path to obtain codes without first disabling 2FA via the working authenticator they are trying to recover from. The entire pre-deploy 2FA population — the users most likely to need the lost-access flow — gets MissingBackupCodes from both new backup-code paths and no self-serve remedy, making the feature inert for exactly its highest-value audience.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds two behavior-bearing backend paths — backup-code verification plus consume-on-use re-encryption in authorize(), and the backupCode branch of the disable endpoint — with zero tests, and the added TODO explicitly admits login and disable-with-backup are untested. A regression in the consumption write (dropping the re-encrypt, or the dash-stripping comparison) makes backup codes silently replayable forever or locks out lost-access users while the existing 2FA e2e suite stays green, since the test file already has the codes from the setup response and never exercises them.

[ADVISORY] The diff bundles tabIndex={-1} on the shared PasswordField visibility toggle — an app-wide keyboard-navigation change affecting every password input in the product — into a 2FA backup-codes PR, with no backup-code requirement it traces to. Keyboard-only users lose tab access to the show/hide control on all password fields product-wide, and because the change rides in an unrelated security PR it cannot be bisected or reverted independently when the a11y regression is reported.

[BUG] The diff removes onEnable() from the successful-enable handler and defers it to the backup-codes Close button (lines 261-272), so the dialog's built-in X (wired to onOpenChange) at the DisplayBackupCodes step exits without ever notifying the parent that 2FA was enabled. A user who enables 2FA and dismisses the codes screen via X leaves the settings page showing the 2FA switch unchecked while 2FA is in fact enabled server-side, and may re-attempt setup or misjudge their account's security state from the stale UI.

[BUG] The login page collects backupCode (registered by the new BackupCode component, typed in LoginValues) but the diff never transmits it: neither the zod formSchema behind zodResolver (untouched by any hunk, and zodResolver strips keys absent from the schema out of the submitted data) nor the signIn('credentials', ...) payload in handleSignIn (no hunk touches that call) is updated, so credentials.backupCode is always undefined in authorize() and the lost-access login branch is unreachable. A user who lost their authenticator and enters a valid backup code is bounced back to the TOTP prompt with SecondFactorRequired forever — the feature's primary recovery flow authenticates no one, and the diff's own e2e TODO confirms login-with-backup is untested, so nothing catches it.

[BUG] Backup-code consumption in authorize() is an unguarded read-modify-write: the array is read and decrypted, matched with indexOf, nulled in memory, and the whole blob rewritten with no unique constraint, version column, or conditional update, so two concurrent sign-ins presenting the same code both pass. Two parallel POSTs to the auth callback with one backup code both create sessions — the 'used exactly once' invariant the UI explicitly promises ('Each backup code can be used exactly once') is violated, and concurrent logins with different codes resurrect already-consumed codes via lost update, leaving burned codes valid for later replay.

[ADVISORY] Storing all backup codes as a single encrypted JSON TEXT blob on User is the wrong data structure for single-use consumption: the column cannot enforce per-code uniqueness, cannot expose per-code used-state to the database, and forces whole-blob read-modify-write on every use. This shape is the direct enabler of the TOCTOU in authorize() — a BackupCode child table (hashed code, UNIQUE(user, code), atomic UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL checking rowCount) would make single-use enforceable at the data layer; with the blob it is unenforceable without application locking.

[ADVISORY] The MissingBackupCodes error tells users to generate codes in their settings, but backup codes are generated exclusively inside setup.ts's enable-2FA flow — no settings path anywhere in the diff can generate or re-display codes, so the remediation the error text instructs is impossible to perform. Every user who enabled 2FA before this feature shipped (backupCodes null) — exactly the population most likely to have lost their authenticator — gets a dead-end message on lost-access login; obtaining codes requires disabling 2FA, which itself requires the TOTP they lost, so lost-access users are fully locked out.

[ADVISORY] onEnable is no longer called when enable succeeds (the success handler now only advances the step) — the callback fires solely from the new DisplayBackupCodes 'close' button, so closing the modal via esc/X/overlay after enabling skips both resetState and onEnable. The parent settings component's 2FA switch state is left stale because its only refresh signal was onEnable, and since the codes exist only in modal React state with no re-view path, an accidental esc at the codes step permanently destroys the only presentation of codes that are already persisted and active.

[ADVISORY] The twoFactorLostAccess toggle and typed form values survive modal close because resetForm is wired only to the custom toggle/success paths — the cancel button (onCancel) and Dialog onOpenChange reset nothing. A user who toggles 'lost access', cancels, and reopens the modal finds it still in backup-code mode with the previously typed (possibly rejected) code and stale error state — stale auth inputs on a security-sensitive form, since the wrapper component stays mounted across open/close cycles.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code format is re-encoded as bare magic numbers in five files with no shared constant: setup.ts (Array(10), randomBytes(5) — under a comment that misstates '10 character length' when the line generates ten 10-char codes), BackupCode.tsx (minLength 10/maxLength 11), EnableTwoFactorModal (slice(0,5)/slice(5,10)), and the dash-stripping comparisons in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts. A future change to code length or format (e.g., an entropy hardening) must be synchronized across five sites; missing one makes the input reject valid codes or makes the server comparison unable to match what was stored — a silent login failure on an auth path that has no test coverage in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The new BackupCode.tsx component's function is declared as `export default function TwoFactor` — the codebase now has two default-exported components named TwoFactor with adjacent auth semantics. A maintainer grepping or navigating by component name to change TOTP behavior lands on the backup-code component (and vice versa), so the next edit targets the wrong component.

[BUG] The pre-toggle 2FA assertion `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` checks the truthiness of a Promise object and therefore always passes — the diff's own added FIXME admits this ('this passes even when switch is not checked') yet ships the broken assertion unchanged. The e2e suite claims to verify the 2FA switch's initial unchecked state while asserting nothing, so any regression in that state stays green — the diff documents a false guard instead of fixing it.

[ADVISORY] Both server-side backup-code verification paths (authorize() in next-auth-options.ts and the disable endpoint) plus the login-page wiring ship with zero test coverage — the diff's own TODO ('add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup') names exactly the untested behaviors. The dead login path (backupCode never transmitted to signIn) sits precisely inside the untested region and shipped undetected; a regression in either verification branch breaks lost-access recovery with nothing failing in CI.

[ADVISORY] body.backupCodes is used unguarded (setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes) immediately followed by body.backupCodes.map(...)), but during a rolling deploy a user's page can be served by a new pod while their setup XHR is routed to an old pod whose setup.ts response predates the field. In the deploy window a 200 setup response lacking backupCodes throws TypeError at the Blob construction (caught as a generic error), so 2FA setup fails spuriously for users mid-deploy even though the server already rotated their secret.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code decrypt/normalize/match logic is implemented twice by hand — once here and once in next-auth-options.ts — with the consumption difference maintained only by an inline comment and no shared module. The two copies of this security check drift independently: a normalization or hardening fix (case folding, trimming, attempt limiting) applied to one path leaves the other silently divergent, with no single source of truth for what a valid backup-code match means.

[BUG] The backupCode value typed into the login form never reaches authorize(): this diff adds backupCode to LoginValues and registers the input, but no hunk in this PR adds backupCode to the zod formSchema driving zodResolver (z.object strips unknown keys from the parsed values handed to handleSignIn) nor to the unchanged signIn() call inside handleSignIn, so credentials.backupCode in next-auth-options.ts is always undefined. A user who lost their authenticator enters a valid backup code, the stripped submission makes authorize() fall into the TOTP branch and return second-factor-required, so the backup-code login path — the feature this PR exists to deliver — silently no-ops and the user is locked out; the diff's own TODO (login.2fa.e2e.ts line 11) confirms no test exercises this path, so CI cannot catch it.

[BUG] Replacing onEnable() with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes) at line 135 silently changes the modal's output contract: the parent is now notified that 2FA was enabled only when the user clicks the new close button (line 269), not when the enable API succeeds. A user who enables 2FA and then dismisses the backup-codes screen via Escape or the dialog's X (the onOpenChange path, which never routes through the close button's onClick) triggers no onEnable() call, leaving the settings page showing 2FA as disabled while the account now demands a second factor at next login — a state desync the original immediate-callback design made impossible.

[BUG] The MissingBackupCodes guard at line 137 tests !user.backupCodes, but the single-use consumption logic at line 148 writes back "[null,...]" after the tenth use, so an exhausted user passes the guard, hits the indexOf check at line 144, and receives IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes. A user who consumed all ten single-use codes and then lost the authenticator is told "Backup code is incorrect" rather than that no codes remain, prompting endless re-entry of codes that can never validate instead of escalation to account recovery.

[BUG] The disable endpoint's !user.backupCodes check at line 54 misses the exhausted state because consumed codes are persisted as a truthy "[null,...]" JSON array, so the user falls through to indexOf at line 61 and gets IncorrectBackupCode at line 63 instead of MissingBackupCodes. A user relying on this endpoint as their last self-service recovery path with exhausted codes gets a misleading "incorrect code" error that hides the true state and the fact that only support intervention remains.

[ADVISORY] The missing_backup_codes message instructs users to "generate them in your settings", but this diff ships no settings UI or API that regenerates backup codes for an account with 2FA already enabled — the only generator (setup.ts) is reachable solely from the enable flow, which is gated on 2FA being disabled. Every pre-existing 2FA user (backupCodes null after the migration) who loses their authenticator is directed to perform an action that does not exist anywhere in the product, converting the advertised self-service recovery into a hard lockout with a message that blames the user.

[ADVISORY] The PR's own TODO concedes that the two behaviors the feature exists for — logging in with a backup code and disabling 2FA with a backup code — have no test, while all new e2e coverage targets the backup-codes display dialog. A regression in the authorize() backup branch (next-auth-options.ts lines 131-157) or the disable endpoint's backup branch (disable.ts lines 48-69) locks users out of their accounts with zero CI signal — the value-plumbing defect in the login path is exactly the class of ship-breaking bug this acknowledged gap lets through.

[ADVISORY] The committed FIXME documents that the assertion expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() passes even when the two-factor switch is unchecked, i.e. the step's guard assertion is vacuous. CI green-reports the 2FA-enable step as verified when the author has already documented that it verifies nothing, so a regression leaving the switch unchecked is masked at the exact assertion meant to catch it, and future readers trust a check known to be meaningless.

[BUG] tabIndex={-1} on the password-visibility toggle (line 49) removes the control from sequential keyboard focus for every PasswordField in the application, with no alternative keyboard activation path added. Keyboard-only users across login, signup, and every settings password field can no longer tab to or activate the show/hide password button — an app-wide WCAG 2.1.1 accessibility regression bundled into a 2FA PR with no connection to its stated objective and no explicit acceptance.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code verification core (decrypt, JSON.parse, dash-stripping indexOf) is copy-pasted between authorize() here and the disable endpoint (disable.ts lines 58-61) instead of extracted, with the copies already diverging in consumption semantics (this copy nulls the used code at line 148; the disable copy defers to the final wipe). The next maintainer who changes code format, length, or normalization (e.g. case folding) in one copy leaves the other accepting or rejecting inconsistently, so a code that validates at login fails at disable or vice versa — silent divergence in the highest-consequence logic in the feature.

[ADVISORY] The new backup-code component is declared as `export default function TwoFactor(...)` — copy-paste residue leaving the function named TwoFactor while the file and every import site call it BackupCode. React DevTools, the profiler, and stack traces show two different components both named TwoFactor on the login and disable-2FA screens, so anyone triaging an auth incident or grepping for the BackupCode component definition misidentifies which component rendered the field.

[BUG] Backup-code single-use enforcement in authorize() is a non-atomic read-modify-write: backupCodes.indexOf(...) on the freshly decrypted list gates an unconditional prisma.user.update that rewrites the entire list, with no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the ciphertext. Two concurrent sign-ins presenting the same backup code both read the pre-update list, both pass the indexOf check, and both receive sessions — a double-submitted login form or an attacker racing a phished code gets a second session from a code the user believes is burned; worse, interleaved use of two different codes resurrects an already-consumed code (each request writes back a list derived from the pre-update state, so the later write restores the other request's code to valid), violating the 'Each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee the new locale string states.

[ADVISORY] The diff wires the BackupCode input, the server-side credentials.backupCode branch in next-auth-options.ts, and client-side handling for IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes, but no hunk in the diff adds backupCode to the signIn('calcom', ...) credentials payload in handleSignIn — the pre-existing call passes only email, password, and totpCode — so the field the new authorize() branch requires is never transmitted from the login page. A user who lost their authenticator clicks 'Lost access', enters a valid backup code, and the credentials provider receives no backupCode, so the TOTP branch answers SecondFactorRequired instead of authenticating: the login recovery path — the core purpose of the PR — is inert and the two new error branches at lines 157-158 are unreachable dead code; the PR's own e2e TODO ('add more backup code tests, e.g. login ... with backup') shows this path was never exercised.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code verification algorithm (symmetricDecrypt with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, then JSON.parse, then indexOf of the dash-stripped input) is hand-duplicated between this endpoint and the credentials authorize() in next-auth-options.ts, and the copies already drift: this disable endpoint's error log says 'cannot proceed with backup code login', copy-pasted from the login flow. The next change to backup-code verification — switching to hashed storage after a key-compromise review, adding case/format normalization, or changing code length — must be applied in two hand-maintained places; updating only the login copy leaves disable accepting codes login rejects (or vice versa), producing inconsistent authentication behavior on a security control enforced independently by two endpoints.

[ADVISORY] The login page surfaces the MissingBackupCodes message — 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' — to a user who is, by construction, unable to authenticate to reach those settings. Pre-feature 2FA users (backupCodes null after the migration) who lost their authenticator follow 'Lost access', submit a code, and are told to perform an action requiring the exact login they just failed — a recovery dead-end that sends locked-out users hunting for a screen they cannot open instead of directing them to account recovery support.

[BUG] showToast(t('backup_codes_copied'), 'success') runs synchronously on the line after the un-awaited navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) promise, so the success toast is displayed regardless of whether the clipboard write resolves or rejects. A user whose clipboard write rejects — Firefox with the clipboard permission denied for the site, or an embedded webview without a clipboard grant — is told their one-time recovery codes were copied when they were not; they close the dialog relying on an empty clipboard and are permanently locked out when they later lose their authenticator, while the e2e test only asserts the toast appears and cannot catch the failure.

[BUG] The enable-2FA e2e's switch-state assertion `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` (line 53) asserts an un-awaited Promise object, which is always truthy, so it passes unconditionally — the FIXME comment this same diff adds at lines 50-51 ("this passes even when switch is not checked") documents the tautology and the broken assertion is left in place. The step that reads as verifying 2FA was enabled verifies nothing: a regression that leaves the switch off (broken toggle handler, failed enable) is still green at this assertion, and real coverage of the checked state rests entirely on the later data-state="checked" selector at line 127 — every maintainer reading this test is handed false confidence that enablement is asserted mid-flow.

[BUG] The new backup-codes block declares "backup codes are now showing, so run a few tests" but never asserts a single code is rendered: line 116 checks only download.suggestedFilename(), which comes from the hardcoded download="cal-backup-codes.txt" anchor attribute in EnableTwoFactorModal and is independent of blob content, and line 121 waits only for a toast-success testid that the copy handler shows unconditionally right after the un-awaited navigator.clipboard.writeText call (the diff's own TODOs at lines 117 and 122 admit file and clipboard content go unchecked). The suite cannot distinguish a user who received 10 valid codes from one who received zero: if setup.ts's generation regresses to an empty array (or codes of wrong length/format), the grid renders nothing, the downloaded file is empty, the clipboard gets an empty string, and this e2e stays fully green — and because codes are displayed exactly once and never retrievable afterward, affected users have no recovery path when they lose their authenticator, with no CI signal.

[ADVISORY] The new backup-code login verification — decrypt, dash-stripped indexOf match (line 144), and single-use consumption via `backupCodes[index] = null` plus re-encrypt (lines 148-156), implementing the "used exactly once" guarantee stated in this diff's own backup_code_instructions locale string — is exercised by no test: I checked apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts (the only 2FA test file changed; its new lines 110-125 only click the settings-modal download/copy/close buttons) and packages/lib/test/builder.ts (adds only a `backupCodes: null` fixture default), and neither ever submits a backupCode to login nor asserts consumption; the diff's own TODO at login.2fa.e2e.ts:13 concedes login-with-backup tests are missing. The feature's central security guarantee ships unverified: a regression in this block — e.g. re-encrypting the array before nulling the matched index, or dropping the replaceAll('-', '') so formatted user input never matches — leaves CI green while either spent codes remain reusable indefinitely or every valid backup code is rejected, locking out precisely the users who lost their authenticator and have no other second factor.

[ADVISORY] The new disable-with-backup-code branch — the raw `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset (line 51), the MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode error paths (lines 54-63), and the backupCodes: null clear added at line 107 — is triggered by no test: login.2fa.e2e.ts (the only changed 2FA test file, checked alongside packages/lib/test/builder.ts) drives the disable endpoint only through the TOTP path and never clicks the new "lost access" toggle in DisableTwoFactorModal, and the diff's TODO at login.2fa.e2e.ts:13 lists "disabling 2fa with backup" as outstanding. Regressions on this branch ship unobserved: with the encryption key unset the handler crashes into a 500 instead of the 4xx the new error-code contract promises, and a decrypt/match bug means users who lost their authenticator can never disable 2FA (or disable succeeds while the intended backupCodes clear silently stops happening) — all with a green suite, because no test ever posts a backupCode to this endpoint.

[BUG] The login page never forwards backupCode to the credentials provider: the nextAuthSignIn call site between this diff's hunks (lines ~136-152, unchanged from the review base which predates backup codes) still destructures only email/password/totpCode, so credentials.backupCode is always undefined and the IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes branches added here are unreachable dead code. A user who clicks 'Lost access' and submits a valid backup code gets no error and no session — authorize skips the backup branch, sees an empty totpCode, and throws SecondFactorRequired, silently re-arming the TOTP prompt — so backup-code login, the PR's core recovery flow, is dead on arrival in production and ships untested (the e2e TODO explicitly skips login-with-backup).

[ADVISORY] The migration adds backupCodes as NULL for every existing row and this setup call is the only writer in the entire diff — there is no backfill, no regenerate endpoint, no settings action, and no re-display path, so existing twoFactorEnabled users and anyone who misses the one-shot codes dialog can never obtain or replenish codes. [ADVISORY] The default export of BackupCode.tsx is declared as `function TwoFactor({ center = true })`, giving two distinct components named TwoFactor that DisableTwoFactorModal and login.tsx import together and switch between. React DevTools, stack traces, and grep for "TwoFactor" show the TOTP component when a developer is debugging the backup-code path on this security-critical screen, raising the risk of editing or instrumenting the wrong component during the next change.
matched_golden_ids: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that BackupCode.tsx exports a component/function named `TwoFactor`, creating inconsistent/misleading naming (backup-code component named TwoFactor) and confusion because there are multiple `TwoFactor` components used in the flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds backupCode to LoginValues and registers the field in the form, but never adds backupCode to the zod formSchema that zodResolver (unchanged context at login.tsx:67) applies to every submission, so the parsed values handed to signIn("credentials") omit the key. authorize() never sees credentials.backupCode, always takes the TOTP branch, and returns SecondFactorRequired on every lost-access attempt — the backup-code login flow this PR builds can never authenticate, and the UI shows no error because SecondFactorRequired merely re-sets the already-true twoFactorRequired flag.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx the diff adds `backupCode` to `LoginValues` and introduces a UI path that registers/uses it via `<BackupCode />` and `methods.setValue("backupCode", "")`. However, the form still uses `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })` and the diff shows no corresponding update to `formSchema` to include `backupCode`. With Zod's default object parsing behavior (unknown keys are typically stripped unless `.passthrough()` is used), this can result in `backupCode` being omitted from the submitted values, meaning `signIn("credentials")` would never send it and `authorize()` would not enter the `credentials.backupCode` branch. This would break the new lost-access backup-code login path and may surface as repeated `SecondFactorRequired` without a new error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The MissingBackupCodes error copy instructs users to "generate them in your settings", but this diff ships no settings UI or API that generates or regenerates backup codes — the only generator is the setup endpoint, which runs exclusively when starting a fresh 2FA enable. Users who hit this error (anyone who exhausted, lost, or was never given their codes) follow the instruction, find no such control anywhere in settings, and dead-end in the recovery flow this PR advertises; support intervention becomes the only exit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` and the user-facing copy `"missing_backup_codes": "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."` (common.json). The only place backup codes are generated in this diff is the 2FA setup endpoint (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` generates and stores `backupCodes`), which is used during the enable-2FA flow. There is no separate settings UI or API in the diff to generate/regenerate backup codes for users who already have 2FA enabled but have `backupCodes` missing/null (a case explicitly handled in both login authorize and disable endpoint). So the instruction to “generate them in your settings” is not supported by any new control/endpoint shown here; it’s a scope/UX gap rather than a direct functional crash/bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The single-use invariant this PR itself states in its shipped copy ("Each backup code can be used exactly once") is enforced as a non-atomic check-then-write: indexOf runs against the decrypted array and the nulled array is persisted in a separate unconditional prisma.user.update with no condition on the code. Two concurrent sign-ins submitting the same code both pass the indexOf check before either write lands, so the code authenticates twice (or N times in a burst) while the updates clobber each other — a replayed/phished code keeps working in the race window regardless of the victim consuming it.
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same race condition: backup codes are checked in decrypted in-memory array and then updated in a separate non-atomic write, allowing concurrent logins with the same code to both pass and effectively reuse a one-time code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration adds backupCodes as a nullable column with no backfill, so every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy keeps backupCodes null and has no path to obtain codes without first disabling 2FA via the working authenticator they are trying to recover from. The entire pre-deploy 2FA population — the users most likely to need the lost-access flow — gets MissingBackupCodes from both new backup-code paths and no self-serve remedy, making the feature inert for exactly its highest-value audience.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nullable `backupCodes` column (migration + Prisma schema) and only populates it during the new 2FA setup flow (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` updates `backupCodes`). The new “lost access” paths in login (`credentials.backupCode` in `next-auth-options.ts`) and disable (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` when `req.body.backupCode`) explicitly error with `MissingBackupCodes` when `user.backupCodes` is null. There is no diff-shown backfill or separate “generate backup codes” flow for existing 2FA-enabled users, so pre-deploy 2FA users will hit `MissingBackupCodes` if they try the new backup-code recovery path. This is a real rollout/product gap grounded in the diff, though not a runtime correctness bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds two behavior-bearing backend paths — backup-code verification plus consume-on-use re-encryption in authorize(), and the backupCode branch of the disable endpoint — with zero tests, and the added TODO explicitly admits login and disable-with-backup are untested. A regression in the consumption write (dropping the re-encrypt, or the dash-stripping comparison) makes backup codes silently replayable forever or locks out lost-access users while the existing 2FA e2e suite stays green, since the test file already has the codes from the setup response and never exercises them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial, behavior-bearing backup-code logic in two backend paths without adding coverage that exercises it: (1) next-auth authorize() adds a `credentials.backupCode` branch that dash-strips (`replaceAll("-", "")`), validates against decrypted `user.backupCodes`, then consumes by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting via `symmetricEncrypt(...)` (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts). (2) The disable endpoint adds a `req.body.backupCode` branch that validates against decrypted stored codes but does not have any accompanying tests (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts). The Playwright suite explicitly notes missing backup-code tests (`// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`) and the added e2e flow only tests display/copy/download/close of backup codes, not using them to login or disable 2FA (apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts). This makes the review concern specific and diff-grounded (risk of regressions in consume-on-use, dash handling, or backup-code disable path going undetected), but it’s not itself a verifiable defect in the diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff bundles tabIndex={-1} on the shared PasswordField visibility toggle — an app-wide keyboard-navigation change affecting every password input in the product — into a 2FA backup-codes PR, with no backup-code requirement it traces to. Keyboard-only users lose tab access to the show/hide control on all password fields product-wide, and because the change rides in an unrelated security PR it cannot be bisected or reverted independently when the a11y regression is reported.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared `PasswordField` visibility-toggle `<button>` in `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx` to `tabIndex={-1}`. That removes the toggle control from the keyboard tab order across the product, so keyboard-only users can no longer focus/activate the show/hide password control on any password field. This is a concrete, app-wide behavior/accessibility regression introduced by this PR, regardless of the PR’s 2FA/backup-code feature scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff removes onEnable() from the successful-enable handler and defers it to the backup-codes Close button (lines 261-272), so the dialog's built-in X (wired to onOpenChange) at the DisplayBackupCodes step exits without ever notifying the parent that 2FA was enabled. A user who enables 2FA and dismisses the codes screen via X leaves the settings page showing the 2FA switch unchecked while 2FA is in fact enabled server-side, and may re-attempt setup or misjudge their account's security state from the stale UI.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, the successful enable handler no longer calls onEnable(); it now does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` on HTTP 200 (around the former onEnable call). The only place onEnable() is invoked afterward is the "Close" button inside the DisplayBackupCodes step (data-testid="backup-codes-close"), which also calls resetState(). However the Dialog is controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`, so dismissing the modal via the built-in X (triggering onOpenChange) at the DisplayBackupCodes step will close the dialog without calling onEnable() or resetState(), leaving the parent/settings UI potentially stale (e.g., 2FA switch still unchecked) even though 2FA was enabled server-side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The login page collects backupCode (registered by the new BackupCode component, typed in LoginValues) but the diff never transmits it: neither the zod formSchema behind zodResolver (untouched by any hunk, and zodResolver strips keys absent from the schema out of the submitted data) nor the signIn('credentials', ...) payload in handleSignIn (no hunk touches that call) is updated, so credentials.backupCode is always undefined in authorize() and the lost-access login branch is unreachable. A user who lost their authenticator and enters a valid backup code is bounced back to the TOTP prompt with SecondFactorRequired forever — the feature's primary recovery flow authenticates no one, and the diff's own e2e TODO confirms login-with-backup is untested, so nothing catches it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `backupCode` field end-to-end (UI via `BackupCode` registering `backupCode`, NextAuth `authorize()` consuming `credentials.backupCode`, and new error handling for `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` in `login.tsx`). However, within the shown `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` changes, only the UI state/conditional rendering was updated; there are no corresponding hunks updating the zod `formSchema` used by `zodResolver(formSchema)` or the `signIn('credentials', ...)` payload to ensure `backupCode` is actually included in submitted credentials. Given zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default, if `formSchema` wasn’t updated elsewhere, `backupCode` would be dropped and `credentials.backupCode` would remain undefined, making the backup-code login path unreachable and causing users to keep hitting `SecondFactorRequired`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Backup-code consumption in authorize() is an unguarded read-modify-write: the array is read and decrypted, matched with indexOf, nulled in memory, and the whole blob rewritten with no unique constraint, version column, or conditional update, so two concurrent sign-ins presenting the same code both pass. Two parallel POSTs to the auth callback with one backup code both create sessions — the 'used exactly once' invariant the UI explicitly promises ('Each backup code can be used exactly once') is violated, and concurrent logins with different codes resurrect already-consumed codes via lost update, leaving burned codes valid for later replay.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code validation/consumption is implemented as a non-atomic read-modify-write: decrypt `user.backupCodes`, `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, then mutate `backupCodes[index] = null` and write the entire encrypted blob back via `prisma.user.update(...)` with no conditional/transactional guard. The diff shows no unique constraint, version check, `where` clause asserting the old value, or DB-side atomic operation, so concurrent auth requests can both validate against the same pre-update state and both succeed, and concurrent updates with different codes can overwrite each other (lost update), potentially reintroducing already-consumed codes. This violates the UI promise added in `common.json` ("Each backup code can be used exactly once").

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Storing all backup codes as a single encrypted JSON TEXT blob on User is the wrong data structure for single-use consumption: the column cannot enforce per-code uniqueness, cannot expose per-code used-state to the database, and forces whole-blob read-modify-write on every use. This shape is the direct enabler of the TOCTOU in authorize() — a BackupCode child table (hashed code, UNIQUE(user, code), atomic UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL checking rowCount) would make single-use enforceable at the data layer; with the blob it is unenforceable without application locking.

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores backup codes as a single encrypted JSON blob on `User.backupCodes` (schema + setup endpoint), and login consumes a code via a read-modify-write in `authorize()` (decrypt JSON → `indexOf` match → `backupCodes[index] = null` → `prisma.user.update(...)`). This update is not conditional/atomic on the matched code still being unused, so two concurrent login attempts with the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf(...)` check before either write commits (TOCTOU), violating the intended single-use property. The blob structure also prevents enforcing per-code uniqueness/used-state at the DB layer, making single-use unenforceable without additional locking/atomic DB primitives.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The MissingBackupCodes error tells users to generate codes in their settings, but backup codes are generated exclusively inside setup.ts's enable-2FA flow — no settings path anywhere in the diff can generate or re-display codes, so the remediation the error text instructs is impossible to perform. Every user who enabled 2FA before this feature shipped (backupCodes null) — exactly the population most likely to have lost their authenticator — gets a dead-end message on lost-access login; obtaining codes requires disabling 2FA, which itself requires the TOTP they lost, so lost-access users are fully locked out.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a “Lost access” backup-code login path (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx renders <BackupCode> and next-auth authorize() accepts credentials.backupCode), but both login (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts) and disable-2FA (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts) hard-fail with ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes when user.backupCodes is null. Backup codes are only generated in the 2FA setup endpoint (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts) which is reached via the settings enable-2FA flow (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx) and requires being logged in. There is no other code path in the diff that can generate/re-display backup codes for already-2FA-enabled users, so users who enabled 2FA before this change (backupCodes null) and have lost their authenticator are led to an impossible remediation (common.json: “Please generate them in your settings.”) and are effectively locked out.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] onEnable is no longer called when enable succeeds (the success handler now only advances the step) — the callback fires solely from the new DisplayBackupCodes 'close' button, so closing the modal via esc/X/overlay after enabling skips both resetState and onEnable. The parent settings component's 2FA switch state is left stale because its only refresh signal was onEnable, and since the codes exist only in modal React state with no re-view path, an accidental esc at the codes step permanently destroys the only presentation of codes that are already persisted and active.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, the successful enable handler no longer calls onEnable; it now only does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, response.status===200 in handleEnable). The only place that calls `onEnable()` after enabling is the DisplayBackupCodes “close” button handler (data-testid="backup-codes-close"). There is no reset/onEnable wiring in `Dialog`’s `onOpenChange`, so dismissing the modal via ESC/X/overlay at the backup-codes step will close it without calling `onEnable()` and without `resetState()`. Since backup codes are only displayed from modal state (`backupCodes` set from /setup response) and there’s no re-fetch/re-display path shown in this diff, an accidental dismissal can lose the only presentation of already-generated codes, and the parent relying on onEnable to refresh 2FA state can remain stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The twoFactorLostAccess toggle and typed form values survive modal close because resetForm is wired only to the custom toggle/success paths — the cancel button (onCancel) and Dialog onOpenChange reset nothing. A user who toggles 'lost access', cancels, and reopens the modal finds it still in backup-code mode with the previously typed (possibly rejected) code and stale error state — stale auth inputs on a security-sensitive form, since the wrapper component stays mounted across open/close cycles.

adjudication.rationale: In DisableTwoFactorModal, new state `twoFactorLostAccess` and form values (`backupCode`, `totpCode`, `password`) are only cleared via `resetForm()` on success and via the lost-access toggle button (`onClick` calls `resetForm(false)`). The cancel button still calls only `onCancel` (no `resetForm`, no `setTwoFactorLostAccess(false)`) and there’s no other reset on close shown. If the modal component remains mounted when closed (common for controlled dialogs), reopening would preserve the backup-code mode, previously typed codes, and `errorMessage` state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The backup-code format is re-encoded as bare magic numbers in five files with no shared constant: setup.ts (Array(10), randomBytes(5) — under a comment that misstates '10 character length' when the line generates ten 10-char codes), BackupCode.tsx (minLength 10/maxLength 11), EnableTwoFactorModal (slice(0,5)/slice(5,10)), and the dash-stripping comparisons in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts. A future change to code length or format (e.g., an entropy hardening) must be synchronized across five sites; missing one makes the input reject valid codes or makes the server comparison unable to match what was stored — a silent login failure on an auth path that has no test coverage in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes the backup-code structure in multiple places: generation in `setup.ts` uses `Array.from(Array(10), ...)` with `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` (10 hex chars per code), UI input constraints in `BackupCode.tsx` use `minLength={10}` / `maxLength={11}` with a `XXXXX-XXXXX` placeholder, display formatting in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` uses `slice(0, 5)` / `slice(5, 10)`, and server-side matching strips dashes via `.replaceAll("-", "")` in both `next-auth-options.ts` and `pages/api/.../disable.ts`. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/coupling issue: any future format/length change must be synchronized across these sites or else valid codes could be rejected/mismatched. However, it does not demonstrate a current, verifiable defect introduced by the diff (the current constants are internally consistent for 10-char codes optionally displayed with a dash). The finding’s claim that the setup.ts comment is wrong is not supported by the diff (it does generate 10-character codes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new BackupCode.tsx component's function is declared as `export default function TwoFactor` — the codebase now has two default-exported components named TwoFactor with adjacent auth semantics. A maintainer grepping or navigating by component name to change TOTP behavior lands on the backup-code component (and vice versa), so the next edit targets the wrong component.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx` defines `export default function TwoFactor({ center = true }) { ... }`, while `apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx` also default-exports a `TwoFactor` function. Although imports use the file name (`import BackupCode from ...`) so runtime behavior isn’t broken, this duplicate component/function name is diff-grounded and can cause real maintenance/debugging confusion (e.g., grepping, React DevTools showing both as `TwoFactor`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The pre-toggle 2FA assertion `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` checks the truthiness of a Promise object and therefore always passes — the diff's own added FIXME admits this ('this passes even when switch is not checked') yet ships the broken assertion unchanged. The e2e suite claims to verify the 2FA switch's initial unchecked state while asserting nothing, so any regression in that state stays green — the diff documents a false guard instead of fixing it.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the assertion `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` passes a `Promise<boolean>` (from `isChecked()`) into Jest-style `expect`, so `toBeTruthy()` evaluates the Promise object’s truthiness (always truthy) rather than the resolved boolean. The diff even adds a FIXME noting it “passes even when switch is not checked,” and it does not change the assertion to `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or `expect(await locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`, leaving a real false-positive test guard in place.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both server-side backup-code verification paths (authorize() in next-auth-options.ts and the disable endpoint) plus the login-page wiring ship with zero test coverage — the diff's own TODO ('add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup') names exactly the untested behaviors. The dead login path (backupCode never transmitted to signIn) sits precisely inside the untested region and shipped undetected; a regression in either verification branch breaks lost-access recovery with nothing failing in CI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial backup-code flows on both server (next-auth `authorize()` branch handling `credentials.backupCode`, and `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable` handling `req.body.backupCode`) and client (Login + DisableTwoFactorModal UI toggles), but the only test change is in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, which explicitly leaves a TODO to add backup-code tests (e.g. login + disabling 2FA with backup). The added test coverage only exercises backup-code display/copy/download after enabling 2FA, not the verification paths for login/disable. However, the claim that the login path is “dead” because `backupCode` is never transmitted to `signIn` cannot be verified from the shown diff hunks (the `signIn` call isn’t visible here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] body.backupCodes is used unguarded (setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes) immediately followed by body.backupCodes.map(...)), but during a rolling deploy a user's page can be served by a new pod while their setup XHR is routed to an old pod whose setup.ts response predates the field. In the deploy window a 200 setup response lacking backupCodes throws TypeError at the Blob construction (caught as a generic error), so 2FA setup fails spuriously for users mid-deploy even though the server already rotated their secret.

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.handleSetup`, on `response.status === 200` the code does `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and immediately constructs a Blob via `body.backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n")`. If `body.backupCodes` is `undefined` (e.g., a 200 response from an older `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` implementation that didn’t include `backupCodes`), this will throw a `TypeError` at `.map`, breaking 2FA setup in that scenario. The diff shows no guard/fallback for a missing `backupCodes` field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The backup-code decrypt/normalize/match logic is implemented twice by hand — once here and once in next-auth-options.ts — with the consumption difference maintained only by an inline comment and no shared module. The two copies of this security check drift independently: a normalization or hardening fix (case folding, trimming, attempt limiting) applied to one path leaves the other silently divergent, with no single source of truth for what a valid backup-code match means.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate implementations of the backup-code verification logic: in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (decrypt `user.backupCodes`, `JSON.parse`, normalize via `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`, `indexOf` match) and again in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (same decrypt/parse/normalize/match flow on `credentials.backupCode`). They already differ in post-match handling (disable endpoint later nulls all `backupCodes` when disabling 2FA, while next-auth consumes a single code and re-encrypts the remainder by setting `backupCodes[index] = null`). This duplication creates a concrete drift risk for future hardening/normalization changes, but it’s not itself a verifiable functional defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The backupCode value typed into the login form never reaches authorize(): this diff adds backupCode to LoginValues and registers the input, but no hunk in this PR adds backupCode to the zod formSchema driving zodResolver (z.object strips unknown keys from the parsed values handed to handleSignIn) nor to the unchanged signIn() call inside handleSignIn, so credentials.backupCode in next-auth-options.ts is always undefined. A user who lost their authenticator enters a valid backup code, the stripped submission makes authorize() fall into the TOTP branch and return second-factor-required, so the backup-code login path — the feature this PR exists to deliver — silently no-ops and the user is locked out; the diff's own TODO (login.2fa.e2e.ts line 11) confirms no test exercises this path, so CI cannot catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires up a BackupCode input via react-hook-form context (new LoginValues.backupCode and <BackupCode /> which does methods.register("backupCode")), and next-auth authorize() now branches on credentials.backupCode. But within this PR’s login.tsx hunks there is no corresponding change to the zod schema used by zodResolver(formSchema) nor any visible change to the credentials passed to signIn/handleSignIn; if formSchema remains a Zod object without backupCode, zodResolver will return parsed values without that key, so backupCode will never be sent and credentials.backupCode will stay undefined, forcing the TOTP path (SecondFactorRequired) even when a backup code was entered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Replacing onEnable() with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes) at line 135 silently changes the modal's output contract: the parent is now notified that 2FA was enabled only when the user clicks the new close button (line 269), not when the enable API succeeds. A user who enables 2FA and then dismisses the backup-codes screen via Escape or the dialog's X (the onOpenChange path, which never routes through the close button's onClick) triggers no onEnable() call, leaving the settings page showing 2FA as disabled while the account now demands a second factor at next login — a state desync the original immediate-callback design made impossible.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, successful enable no longer calls onEnable() (it now does setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes) in handleEnable’s 200-status branch), and onEnable() is only invoked by the new “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes step. The Dialog’s onOpenChange is passed through to the parent with no internal handler to call onEnable/resetState when the modal is dismissed via other mechanisms (escape, overlay click, or any built-in close control), so it’s possible for 2FA to be enabled server-side while the parent never receives onEnable(). That is a behavioral contract change that can lead to UI state desync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The MissingBackupCodes guard at line 137 tests !user.backupCodes, but the single-use consumption logic at line 148 writes back "[null,...]" after the tenth use, so an exhausted user passes the guard, hits the indexOf check at line 144, and receives IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes. A user who consumed all ten single-use codes and then lost the authenticator is told "Backup code is incorrect" rather than that no codes remain, prompting endless re-entry of codes that can never validate instead of escalation to account recovery.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup-code path checks `if (!user.backupCodes) throw MissingBackupCodes;`, but the consumption logic then sets a used code slot to `null` and re-encrypts the array (`backupCodes[index] = null; ... backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...)`). After all 10 codes are used, `user.backupCodes` remains a non-null encrypted JSON string (e.g., `[null,...]`), so the guard does not trigger. The subsequent `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` will always return `-1` (array contains `null`s), causing `IncorrectBackupCode` instead of a “no codes left”/`MissingBackupCodes`-type error. This matches the finding’s described user-facing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The disable endpoint's !user.backupCodes check at line 54 misses the exhausted state because consumed codes are persisted as a truthy "[null,...]" JSON array, so the user falls through to indexOf at line 61 and gets IncorrectBackupCode at line 63 instead of MissingBackupCodes. A user relying on this endpoint as their last self-service recovery path with exhausted codes gets a misleading "incorrect code" error that hides the true state and the fact that only support intervention remains.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the backup-code path only checks `if (!user.backupCodes)` to emit `MissingBackupCodes`, then decrypts/parses and does `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` to decide `IncorrectBackupCode`. But in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, used backup codes are persisted by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting, so an exhausted set becomes a truthy JSON string like `[null, ...]` rather than `null`. With zodResolver, fields not in the schema are commonly stripped, and without explicit inclusion in the signIn call the backup code will never reach next-auth, making the recovery path ineffective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] handleEnable's success path replaces the onEnable() call with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes), leaving the modal's only success notification wired to the backup-codes Close button, so dismissing the dialog at that step via Escape, the header X, or a backdrop click (all routed to onOpenChange/onCancel) completes the enable server-side without ever notifying the parent. The settings UI keeps showing 2FA as disabled while the account is actually protected; when the user next clicks the switch the setup endpoint re-runs and overwrites the stored backupCodes, silently invalidating the codes the user already saved, and the parent never runs its onEnable side effects (state refresh/query invalidation).

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, the success path of handleEnable was changed from calling onEnable() to only doing setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes) (see response.status === 200 block). The parent callback onEnable is now only invoked by the “Close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes step. However the modal can still be dismissed via the Dialog’s open/onOpenChange mechanism (e.g., Escape/backdrop/header close, depending on Dialog implementation) without triggering onEnable or resetState (resetState is only called in the Cancel button handler and the backup-codes Close handler). That creates a verifiable state-sync hole: 2FA is enabled server-side but the parent may never be notified/refreshed. The diff also shows setup now generates/stores backupCodes on setup; if the UI remains out of sync and the user re-runs setup, it could overwrite stored backup codes, matching the data-loss risk described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Copy button fires navigator.clipboard.writeText without awaiting it and without any rejection handler, then unconditionally shows the 'Backup codes copied!' success toast before the write can complete. When the clipboard write rejects (Firefox without the clipboard-write permission, unfocused document) the user is told the codes were copied when they were not, and on non-HTTPS self-hosted deployments navigator.clipboard is undefined so the handler throws a TypeError and shows no feedback at all — in both cases the user closes the dialog believing the recovery codes are saved and is locked out when they later lose the authenticator.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal’s DisplayBackupCodes step, the Copy button handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without `await`/`.then` and without any error handling, and immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` unconditionally (see `onClick` for `data-testid="backup-codes-copy"`). The diff also doesn’t guard for `navigator.clipboard` being undefined, so in environments where Clipboard API is unavailable/rejected, this can throw or fail while still showing success (or no feedback if it throws), matching the finding’s described incorrect user feedback/behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The backup-code branch of the disable endpoint fails by unhandled throws — a raw Error on a missing CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY and an unguarded symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse of user.backupCodes — instead of the res.status().json({error}) envelope every other branch of this handler returns. These failures surface as non-JSON Next.js 500s; DisableTwoFactorModal unconditionally calls response.json() on non-200 responses, which throws into the generic catch, so the structured IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes mapping is bypassed and the user only sees 'something went wrong' — and after a CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY rotation on a self-hosted instance, every backup-code disable attempt returns an opaque HTML 500 instead of a parseable 4xx JSON error.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing, and it performs `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` with no try/catch. Either condition can produce an unhandled exception and a Next.js 500 (likely non-JSON). On the client, `DisableTwoFactorModal` always does `await response.json()` for non-200 responses; if the server returns HTML/invalid JSON from a 500, that `response.json()` will throw and fall into the generic catch, yielding only `t("something_went_wrong")` and bypassing the structured error mapping (e.g., `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes`). This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The disable endpoint's console.error reports 'Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with backup code login.' on the two-factor disable operation. Operators triaging 2FA-disable failures see them logged as login errors (the string was copy-pasted from next-auth-options.ts where it is accurate), sending debugging to the wrong endpoint and misrepresenting the failed action in any log-based alerting.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the 2FA disable endpoint logs an error message referring to 'backup code login', which misrepresents the operation. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment (login wording used in a disable endpoint).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] authorize() decrypts and JSON.parses user.backupCodes with no guard, so a failed decrypt (rotated CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY since the codes were stored) or corrupted column throws a raw crypto/parse error instead of an ErrorCode. The raw error message propagates as res.error to login.tsx, matches no known error code, and renders as a generic 'something went wrong' — a user attempting backup-code login on a rotated-key instance gets an opaque, unactionable failure on every attempt with nothing distinguishing it in logs from a real auth failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the new backup-code path does `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));` without any try/catch or validation. If `symmetricDecrypt(...)` throws (e.g., wrong/rotated `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) or returns non-JSON (corrupted column), `JSON.parse` will throw a raw runtime/crypto/parse error rather than an `ErrorCode.*`. The surrounding logic only throws `new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes|IncorrectBackupCode|InternalServerError)` for specific checks, so this unguarded throw is a verifiable defect/edge case introduced by the diff that would surface as an unrecognized `res.error` on the client and be rendered as a generic failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read–decrypt–null–re-encrypt–write with no transaction or concurrency guard, so two concurrent sign-ins each read the full code array and last-write-wins resurrects a code the other request already consumed. A user signing in from two devices in quick succession (or a replaying holder of a shoulder-surfed code) double-spends a code the product's own instructions promise 'can be used exactly once', silently breaking the single-use invariant the feature states to users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login does a non-atomic sequence: decrypt `user.backupCodes`, check `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, then mutate `backupCodes[index] = null` and `prisma.user.update(...)` with a re-encrypted JSON blob. There is no transaction/locking or compare-and-swap guard tying the validation to the write. Two concurrent sign-ins can both read the same pre-consumption array and both pass the `index !== -1` check before either write occurs, resulting in two successful authorizations with the same single-use code (and also potential lost-update issues if two different codes are consumed concurrently). This violates the “used exactly once” invariant stated in the UI strings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The missing_backup_codes message instructs 'Please generate them in your settings', but no code path in this product can generate backup codes for an account with 2FA already enabled — codes are only written by the setup endpoint inside the enable flow — and a user receiving this error on the login page cannot reach settings without logging in first. The exact users this error targets — locked-out users without backup codes on the login screen, and disable-modal users sitting in settings — are directed to perform an action that is impossible from where they stand, leaving both audiences with dead-end recovery guidance that masks the absence of any recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `MissingBackupCodes` error and user-facing message `"missing_backup_codes": "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."` (apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json). However, the only place backup codes are generated/stored in this diff is the 2FA setup endpoint `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` which runs during the enable flow and writes `backupCodes` (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts). If a user hits the new backup-code login path with 2FA enabled but `user.backupCodes` is null (possible for existing accounts after the migration), the login/disable flows explicitly return/throw `MissingBackupCodes` (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts; apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts). From the login screen they cannot “generate them in settings” without first authenticating, so the guidance is a dead end for the exact locked-out scenario this error targets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When all ten codes have been consumed, the stored column is the JSON array [null×10] rather than null (consumption writes backupCodes[index] = null), so the !user.backupCodes guard never fires and further attempts throw IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes. A user who exhausted their codes and lost their authenticator is told 'Backup code is incorrect' on every attempt instead of learning that no codes remain, so they keep retrying dead codes instead of seeking account recovery.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code consumption sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and then re-encrypts/stores the JSON array back into `user.backupCodes`. After all codes are used, the DB column still contains an encrypted string representing `[null, null, ...]`, so the guard `if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes);` never triggers. Subsequent attempts decrypt to an array of nulls, `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` returns `-1`, and the code throws `IncorrectBackupCode` rather than indicating that no backup codes remain. This matches the finding's behavior claim.
